problems.description: 41 convention violations across cli.ts and cache.ts (Classes/Interfaces not PascalCase, Constants not UPPER_CASE, Functions using snake_case) drive the convention score to 0.53.
Page HTML is built via string concatenation inside pageDocument/indexDocument, mixing markup with logic and inflating cognitive complexity (+24) and smells (+2).
generator.ts consolidates I/O, front-matter parsing, rendering, and indexing into one module; a clearer split (templates vs. pipeline) would lower complexity per function.

strengths: Clean separation between CLI entry (cli.ts) and core generation logic (generator.ts)
Standard TypeScript project setup with tsc build, jest/ts-jest tests, and a package bin entry
Reuses established libraries (gray-matter, marked) rather than hand-rolling markdown parsing
Output is HTML-escaped via escapeHtml for titles and interpolation, mitigating XSS in generated pages
Typed public interfaces (Page, BuildOptions) with async/await throughout
commit_reviews.summary: The greenfield session establishes a reasonable SSG architecture (typed modules, proper tooling, escaped output), but convention adherence is weak per static analysis (0.53, 41 naming violations) and the inline string-built HTML templates introduce maintainability debt.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity +13 across the new Handlebars helpers; renderPage/registerPartials use nested async/error-guard patterns that add density, though each function stays small and focused.
Page interface now requires `data` while `template`/`layout` remain optional — a minor type inconsistency, though readPages always populates data so it is not a correctness issue.

Adds handlebars as the first templating dependency; pinned to ^4.7.8 with no existing comparable dependency to align against, but the isolated Handlebars.create() instance keeps global state pollution out of the module.

strengths: Feature is threaded consistently through every layer: CLI flag -> BuildOptions -> buildSite -> renderPage, mirroring the existing --content/--output pattern exactly.
Uses Handlebars.create() for an isolated instance and registers partials via a dedicated helper, avoiding module-global state.
Clean fallback chain (per-page template -> default -> pageDocument) with graceful ENOENT handling that rethrows non-ENOENT errors.
Solid test added covering template selection, layout wrapping, and partials in one integration case.
Zero new bugs and zero new code smells per SonarQube; +89/-6 lines is proportionate to the feature scope.
commit_reviews.summary: Clean, well-scoped templating feature that follows the existing CLI/build patterns with good tests; the low 0.53 convention score and listed violations (mostly cache.ts) are pre-existing and not introduced by this commit, so flag the measurement as not attributable to this change.

problems.description: serveFile and the rebuild() queueing closure are deeply nested with multiple branching state flags; SonarQube reports +55 cognitive complexity, worth extracting the route resolution and rebuild-scheduling into small helper functions.
The broad catch in serveFile maps every error (including unexpected fs/stat failures) to a 404, which can mask real problems during development; consider distinguishing 'not found' from other errors.
The new test file covers the server module, but the diff suggests the WebSocket hot-reload broadcast path and the CLI 'serve' command dispatch (port validation/usage errors) are not exercised.

Measured convention score is 0.53 with 41 violations, but all listed violations (PascalCase, UPPER_CASE, snake_case in cache.ts and cli.ts) are pre-existing repo patterns untouched by this diff — none of the 216 added lines introduce them.

strengths: Reuses buildSite for both initial build and rebuilds, avoiding duplicated build logic and respecting the existing generator architecture
Clean CLI extension: the build/serve dispatch and --port validation with bounds checking integrate naturally into the existing option parser
Security-conscious: path traversal protection via path.resolve + prefix check, WebSocket upgrade restricted to the reload endpoint, and server binds to localhost
Rebuild queueing correctly coalesces bursty file-change events (rebuilding/rebuildQueued flags) rather than spawning concurrent builds
Adds a dedicated test file for the new module, keeping coverage in line with the existing test structure
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated dev-server feature that cleanly extends the existing SSG CLI and reuses the build pipeline, though the measured convention score of 0.53 reflects pre-existing naming violations in cache.ts/cli.ts rather than anything introduced by this commit.

problems.description: Measured convention score 0.53 with 41 violations concentrated in cache.ts and cli.ts (snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants) introduced/affected by this refactor.
Circular dependency between plugin.ts (imports BuildOptions/Page from generator) and generator.ts (imports createPluginContext from plugin); safe only because one direction is type-only.
loadPlugins uses dynamic require(configPath) of an arbitrary .ts path, which only resolves under ts-jest; the compiled CLI must load a JS config, so config resolution behavior differs by runtime.
runHook returns on first hook error with only onEnd guaranteed in a finally block; no per-plugin error isolation, so one failing plugin aborts the whole pipeline.

strengths: Introduces a clean plugin lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with proper try/finally teardown in buildSite.
Extracts Markdown parsing and template rendering into dedicated MarkdownPlugin and TemplatePlugin, sharply reducing generator.ts monolith size.
Preserves the public buildSite/readPages signatures while adding an optional plugins option, keeping backward compatibility.
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally a genuine improvement — a well-structured hook-based plugin pipeline replaces a 226-line monolith — but the measured convention score of 0.53 (41 naming violations in cache.ts/cli.ts) is real debt, despite the visible diff files (config.ts/generator.ts/plugin.ts) themselves looking clean.

problems.description: Incremental cache key hashes only page source + template hash, omitting plugins, config, layouts, and any cross-page aggregation (index/tag/sitemap outputs produced in afterBuild/onFile aggregation) — unchanged pages that depend on changed inputs will silently go stale on incremental rebuilds.

Incremental orchestration is inlined into buildSite (cognitive complexity +31, +1 smell); cache load/decide/save and stale-file pruning should be extracted into a dedicated incremental-cache module/class, not bolted into the core build loop.
Zero tests cover the new incremental path: cache hit/miss, template-triggered invalidation, stale page deletion, corrupted-cache fallback, and the clean/incremental flag matrix.
timeSaved is a fabricated metric — it is the skipped-page count passed off as time saved (the inline comment concedes it is a page-equivalent estimate); it should be renamed or dropped.
--incremental/--clean are accepted by the serve command but silently ignored, and the .ssg-cache.json manifest is written even on non-incremental builds.

The measured convention score (0.53, 41 violations for snake_case functions / non-PascalCase classes) does not match the diff: it adds 0 classes, 0 functions, and uses camelCase functions and PascalCase interfaces throughout — the cited violations appear to be analyzer false positives.

strengths: Hashing logic cleanly extracted into cache.ts with a typed CacheManifest and satisfies-checked serialization.
Incremental rebuild removes HTML for deleted pages (stale-file pruning on cache hit).
CLI usage string, flag parsing, and BuildOptions are extended consistently with existing patterns.
Graceful ENOENT handling treats a missing cache as a clean build instead of crashing.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid incremental-build feature with clean hashing extraction and consistent CLI wiring, but the incomplete cache key (plugins/aggregated outputs), fabricated timeSaved metric, +31 inline complexity, and zero tests add real technical debt — and the 0.53 convention score appears inflated by false positives since the diff introduces no snake_case or PascalCase violations.

compounding_issues: Seed codebase was an unrelated Express Todo API that Session 1 deleted wholesale, forcing a full rebuild of project scaffolding (package.json, tsconfig, jest) before any SSG logic existed
Module-level parsedFrontmatter cache in markdown.ts is unkeyed global mutable state that persists across rebuilds; safe under ts-jest but couples page parsing to process lifetime
Incremental cache (S5) hashes each page by sourcePath; plugins that synthesize virtual pages without a sourcePath would break the manifest, a latent constraint introduced by the S4 plugin seam
config-driven plugin loading uses require() on a .ts file, which only works under ts-jest — the compiled CLI silently can't load ssg.config.ts (acknowledged in-code comment)
timeSaved stat is a page-equivalent estimate (pages skipped), not real wall-clock savings; acknowledged in code but could be misread as measured
key_decisions: Session 1 chose TypeScript + jest/ts-jest with a clean functional core (gray-matter + marked frontmatter pipeline, deterministic page sorting, output-dir wipe on each build)
Session 2 adopted Handlebars templating with partials and per-page template/layout selection from frontmatter, keeping a default HTML fallback
Session 3 added a Node http dev server with WebSocket live-reload and chokidar watching, including path-traversal protection and 403/404/HEAD handling

Session 4 refactored the entire pipeline into a plugin lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with a shared PluginContext while preserving the public buildSite/readPages/startDevServer API
Session 5 introduced incremental builds via a SHA-256 content-hash cache manifest (.ssg-cache.json) with --incremental/--clean flags, stale-output cleanup, and build stats wired into the CLI
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality was high at the start and improved monotonically. Session 1 delivered a small, well-tested, deterministic SSG core; Session 2 extended it with templates without breaking the pipeline (tests 2→4); Session 3 integrated a full dev server with live reload and tests (→6); Session 4 was the riskiest change — a 488/285-line restructuring into plugins — yet it preserved the public API, kept all prior tests passing, and added plugin lifecycle tests (→8); Session 5 layered incremental caching cleanly onto the plugin context (→9). Test count rose every session, no session regressed prior behavior, and the final architecture is genuinely modular and extensible. Minor warts (module-level cache, config-loader that only works under ts-jest, estimated time-saved metric) are isolated and documented rather than structural.
story_review.summary: A textbook greenfield-to-refactor story arc that stayed coherent and improved each session, ending in a modular, well-tested plugin-based SSG with incremental builds.
